chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from one who informed him, from Durust ibn Abi Mansur, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said:
Regarding zakat, a man sends it to a land other than his own land. He said: 'There is no harm in him sending one-third or one-fourth.' The doubt is from Abu Ahmad.
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to send zakat to a different country or city than where one lives?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the permissibility of transferring zakat to a region of greater need, specifically allowing the donor to send either one-third or one-fourth of the total amount. The presence of *shakk* (uncertainty) attributed to Abu Ahmad highlights the nuanced transmission chains in Shia hadith scholarship, reflecting the flexibility in calculating the portion to be dispatched when sending zakat abroad.
